method: Current native matcher; cold direction process; same resident cache across all cuts and seeds; off disables completed-fragment retention only; no shared-file snapshot I/O. Matching CPU excludes reduction, audits, verification, publication and preparation.

direct_hits.scope: Identical uncut initial fragment query, warmed cache vs zero retention; includes Python result conversion

limitations: Selected three-case sample, one full-direction observation per arm; not a full-Golden cache-off benchmark.
Extension counts are work counters, not CPU-weighted avoided work.
Warm-hit microbenchmarks include Python result conversion; native branch-search hits do not use that conversion.
Native cache off still performs dependency collection and result accounting; this compares retention, not a separately optimized cache-free implementation.

fragment_pool_replacement.method: Fresh direction process; one native fragment pool across seeds/cuts; zero retention control. All growth decisions execute afresh. Independent reproducible cut/trial streams; canonical saturation representatives independent of existence witness. No event decoding or shared-file exchange in timing controls.
fragment_pool_replacement.limitation: Historical before/after totals use changed random streams and representative ordering, so they are not fixed-workload speedups. Within-replacement on/off comparisons have identical catalogue, scope, graph counts and cap outcomes. This is a selected three-case test, not a full Golden benchmark.

validation.notes: The timing controls preceded removal of unused native cut/placement transport and an explicit selected-path reduction scope correction. Complete-graph controls are unaffected. All final source changes passed the full suite; the additional eviction test was added after collection and run separately.

pipeline_validation.scope: Three selected Golden reactions, both directions, full cut sweep, tolerance 2, branch cap 100, minimum+5 decoding, fresh two-worker local pools at one and ten seeds. Not a full Golden benchmark.
pipeline_validation.timing_scope: Worker stage CPU includes artifact loading and stage execution; decoding includes record materialization. Publication CPU/wall is separate. Matcher CPU is additionally measured within each seed search. Pipeline wall includes startup and publication, but excludes the separately reported decoded-reference audit and post-run parity checks. One observation per seed setting.
pipeline_validation.comparison_scope: All 12 reduced catalogues, matching scopes, graph counts and cap outcomes equal the earlier sequential zero-retention controls. Decoded ground-truth recovery independently replays concrete witnesses from the saved decoded window; it is not inferred from catalogue membership.

indexed_containment.method: Same cold local directions, both directions, all cuts; one fresh previous-implementation baseline, three final pool-on repetitions and one final zero-retention control. Separate matching CPU; no event decoding rerun.

profiling.method: Temporary steady-clock native instrumentation, one ten-seed repetition. Also solve each cache-hit query independently to measure the work avoided and check the proof; those shadow calls do not select returned witnesses. Diagnostic hooks removed before final timings.

limitations: Three selected reactions, not a full Golden rerun.
Baseline timing has one fresh repetition; earlier matching timing was 7.505 s at ten seeds.
Zero retention removes immutable-record sharing as well as existence reuse; its total speedup is not attributable to lookup alone.
Profile phase timings are instrumented wall time; end-to-end reported matching times use the uninstrumented build.

validation.scope: Full suite, including independent matching oracles, containment across 4,097 records, locks, tolerance changes, eviction, snapshots, Python/native parity and work-pool execution.

method: Temporary nested native wall-clock scopes charge each elapsed interval to exactly one phase; no overlapping cumulative timings in the grouped breakdown.
Python seed-graph combination is timed separately. Residual includes cut/seed planning, adapters, bookkeeping, object cleanup and instrumentation overhead outside native scopes.
Separate cProfile run profiles matching only; its inclusive call times identify Python hotspots but must not be added to the exclusive phase table.
Every task is a cold direction process retaining its pool across the full cut sweep. One and ten seeds are compared on identical six-direction scope.
All temporary source changes were restored byte-for-byte, the normal native engine rebuilt, and twelve uninstrumented comparison runs completed.
limitations: Three selected reactions, not a full Golden or EnzymeMap benchmark. No new decoding measurement.
One exclusive-timer repetition, one Python-profile repetition, and one restored uninstrumented repetition; timings are not confidence intervals.

Detailed timers perturb runtime. The ten-seed phase table totals 7.693 seconds wall time; the restored build totals 7.380 seconds CPU and 7.386 seconds wall time. Do not normalize these into an unmeasured exact breakdown of the earlier 7.075-second median.

Atom-set cache identity does not make every raw fragment record interchangeable: anchors, growth constraints and decision context remain attached. Counts establish repeated work, not permission to discard that information.
The earlier 97.5 percent cache success fraction concerns positive queries reaching the pool, excluding immediate direct-extension successes and proven absence.

Runtime identity includes compiled binary bytes and all package Python files; restoration is established by byte-identical scientific source and output audits, not equality to a historical binary fingerprint.
